title: Escalate an Unresponsive Owner
scenario: The gate escalated a blocked task to its owner - and the owner has gone quiet past the deadline. Escalating once is not enough. Design the next rung of the ladder: when the first owner is unresponsive, escalate up with a firmer deadline so a stuck task cannot stall indefinitely.
input: Hire H-4022 has a blocked hardware task. It was escalated to the IT Provisioner with a deadline of SD-2. It is now SD-2 and the IT Provisioner has not responded (level1Responded = false). Ladder rule: if the level-1 owner is unresponsive by the deadline, escalate to the People Ops Lead with a firm final deadline of SD-1. Capture the ladder.
instructions: Record the blocked task and the level-1 owner and deadline.
Record that level 1 did not respond.
Escalate to the level-2 owner (People Ops Lead) with a firm final deadline.
Return one JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Encode an escalation ladder: blockedTask hardware, level1Owner IT Provisioner with level1Deadline SD-2, level1Responded false, escalate to level2Owner People Ops Lead with finalDeadline SD-1.
successMessage: Ladder captured. An unresponsive owner no longer stalls the hire - it climbs to the next rung.
editorHelper: One rung is not a ladder - escalate up when level 1 goes quiet.

sections.title: Owners go quiet
sections.body: At scale, some escalations sit. A single escalation with no next step is a wish, not a mechanism. The ladder is what turns silence into the next accountable person.

sections.title: Each rung is firmer
sections.body: The level-2 deadline (SD-1) is tighter than level 1 because time is running out. Escalation ladders compress as the start date approaches - urgency increases with each rung.

sections.title: Up to whom
sections.body: When the IT Provisioner is unresponsive, the People Ops Lead - who owns the onboarding outcome - is the next rung. The ladder climbs toward broader accountability, not sideways.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A two-rung ladder record: who was asked, that they were silent, and who now owns it with a firm deadline.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd give the owner a deadline, and if they went silent, take it to their lead with a firm date rather than letting it drift.

bestFit.how: create the escalation task with an assignee and a deadline, then notify the owner's manager
a Wait node on the SLA, then a Send node up the ladder when no response arrived

takeaway.heading: Ladder captured
points: You escalated past an unresponsive owner to the next rung.
The level-2 deadline is firmer as the start date nears.
The ladder climbs toward broader accountability (People Ops Lead).
A silent owner no longer stalls the hire indefinitely.
The workflow can now keep a stuck task moving when an owner goes quiet.
